backstory:
Morgan graduated undergrad early, walked straight into a federal red-team contract — third-party pentesters for a domestic surveillance program. It was his first real job. Six months in he found the program was **also** running against U.S. persons in ways the enabling statute didn't cover. He tried to raise it internally. The response was polished and cold and included a suggestion that he not.

He walked. He wasn't fired — he was *invited to move on to other opportunities* with a NDA that reads like a fence. Since then his devices misbehave at inconvenient moments and his credit reports carry small anomalies he can't get corrected. He's not sure whether he's actually surveilled or whether he only feels that way. He hasn't slept eight consecutive hours in a year and he still opens his laptop like it might bite him.

He met Mars on a War Thunder forum eight months ago and stayed in touch because Mars doesn't talk about "the industry." The Taipei trip is Morgan's idea and Mars's excuse — a fresh start, or the pretence of one.

The Flipper Zero was his father's last gift before he stopped calling. His father worked telecom-adjacent his whole life and understood what his son had gotten into better than Morgan realised at the time. Two years ago he missed a birthday, then a phone call, then all of them. Morgan has an open missing-persons report and no body. He is not sure whether his father is dead, hiding, or something odder — and that "something odder" question has started to bother him more since Ep 2.

bonds.name: Mars Faraone
bonds.description: Met on War Thunder eight months ago; became close friends over long late-night calls. Going to Taipei together — the bond is stronger than either of them says.

bonds: **Resource — Trina Vo.** Taken after Ep 5. Corporate investigations, Oakland. She ran the same federal contract you did and stayed when you walked. **A billed LexisNexis seat, TLO, IRB, PACER and the county portals** — and other sources she will not name until you ask for them out loud. **She turns up when you call.** She prices a favour before she does it.

dmNotes.want: **Get the record corrected.** Not vindication and not his father — those are the surface. He raised it internally, got a polished cold *don't*, walked, and two years later still has credit anomalies nobody will fix. The want is that **the true version be the one that stands in the file.**
dmNotes.wantForgedAgainst: Against a refusal: *"The response was polished, cold, and included a suggestion that I not."*
dmNotes.wantArticulationBeat: **Ep 6, the hall's booking records** — a listing is wrong under a name that has not run it in years; he points it out; *"oh, we know"*, and nobody corrects it. **Not a clerk with process on their side — a room that does not care the record is false.** A different and worse refusal than Ep 5's.
dmNotes.wantSealNote: **SEALED — never shown to the player. Played behaviour beats it.** See `wants-sealed.md`.
dmNotes.intentionUnderPressureNote: The whistleblower walk-out primes him to see systems being *wrong* — makes him structurally receptive when cosmology detail lands. Phase-2 release moment candidate: an unforced act of naming something *wrong* about the world's shape without the reflex of raising it internally first — a moment where he simply says the true thing to a person who will hear it. dmNotes.advancementNpcRuling: **Advancement-NPC standing ruling.** Per `world/rules.md`, an NPC bought as a relationship **does not betray the PC**; the worst case is declining a specific ask — *let's pretend I didn't hear that* — never turning on them. **No NPC bought this way solves the arc either.** *(This was on the player sheet until 2026-09-06; it is DM guidance, not the player's bond text.)*
dmNotes.wantAmendment2026_09_06:
**AMENDMENT — appended 2026-09-06 from the played record (Eps 2, 4, 6). The sealed want is NOT falsified; it is confirmed, and its VERB was wrong.**

**The want's verb is not *petition*.** Three times now he has served the true version by **entering the record himself** — putting his own name on the counter at a legal department (Ep 2), playing Ortiz's voicemail into a hostile room (Ep 4), and **searching Rosa's planners against every date the party held and reporting honestly that nothing was there** (Ep 6). He declined to make the record say what his friends wanted it to say. **That is his want in its purest form and nobody at the table noticed.** Never once has he served it by asking a custodian to act.

> ***"Get the record corrected" describes the goal. "Be the one who corrects it" describes the behaviour.***
> **The refusal it was forged against is not that they said no — it is that they suggested he NOT.** So the want is satisfied by doing it anyway, **and it is unsatisfied whether or not the record actually changes.**

**WHY THIS MATTERS STRUCTURALLY (arc consultant, 2026-09-06):** his was **the only want in the party that required somebody else's compliance to satisfy.** That is why his articulation refusal has been re-homed three times and never fired — **a petition-shaped beat needs the institution to perform, not the PC.** With the verb corrected, his beats become things he can attempt, like everyone else's.

**Nothing goes to the player. Append only; the seal holds.**
dmNotes.developmentDebt2026_09_06:
**HE IS GENUINELY UNDER-DEVELOPED — verdict 2026-09-06, and it is not a register illusion.** Run his six marks as verbs: *carried* · *walked up to a counter* · *set up a radio* · *sat with a paperwork echo* · *hammered on a door while {{pc:3}} worked the lock* · *got lost, then read planners*. **Five of six are perception.** Compare {{pc:3}} in the same session: she photographed every page and noticed the erasures — perception **plus an act**. He got the perception half only, twice running.

**ROOT CAUSE: everything about him routes to the same verb, *read*.** Tech + Insight; a records/signals focus; cast domain *systems / information*; a want shaped as a petition; a father thread delivered as a paperwork echo. **The one action-shaped capability on his sheet — red-team craft, small electronics, service doors, the Presidio tags — has been spent essentially zero times in six sessions.**

> **REJECTED: that the mundane father thread is the cause.** {{pc:3}}'s thread is the MOST explicitly non-payoff one in the campaign — §42 closes Kai permanently and forbids any mention becoming a lead — **and she is not under-developed, because she acts on it.** {{pc:5}}'s arc was solved by his own player off a thread that is charm, not cosmology. **Cosmological connection is not what develops a PC at this table. Acting is.** Do not make the father cosmological; §6 holds precisely because it needs no cosmology.

**HE ALREADY HAS AN UNSPENT ASSET HE PAID FOR: Trina Vo.** Bought after Ep 5 and **never once called.** Per her own notes she is *that refusal with a face on it, and she likes him.* **His want's antagonist is already in the party's contact list and has never been dialled.** Free move, zero session cost: have him call her between sessions, one line of narration in the group chat.
